Council Meetings

Ordinary Council Meetings occur on the fourth Tuesday of the month*. (Excluding January and July*)

The next meeting is on 27 October 2026. 

Council meetings are held in the Council Chamber within the Shellharbour Civic Centre. 

Business Papers (Packets) 

Business papers for the next Council meeting will be available from the Thursday prior to the meeting date (see below).

Business papers and minutes for meetings prior to 2015 can be obtained under the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009 by completing an Access to Information form available on the Access to information page. In most cases, documents can be provided in hard copy or electronically.

Attending a Council Meeting

Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. No registration is required to attend.

Before attending a Council meeting, please read the Public Gallery Conduct Standards and Code of Meeting Practice.

Addressing Council (Public Forum)

Addresses to Council (on items listed in the Agenda as Item 10 only) are heard from 4.45pm on the day of the Council Meeting. You can register to speak from the time the Business Paper is published until 10am on the day of the meeting.

To register to speak on a listed matter in the Business Paper under Item 10, complete the  Public Forum Addresses Declaration - Form and return it to Corporate.Meetings@shellharbour.nsw.gov.au before 10am on the day of the meeting. We also encourage you to review the  Public Forum section of our Code of Meeting Practice 

If you are unable to complete the form online, come into or call Council on 4221 6111 and register to speak with a member of staff. You will still need to complete the Declaration prior to addressing Council.

Live streaming and recording

Meetings of the Council are live streamed and recorded. Open the meeting link in the Current Meetings or Previous Meetings for completed meetings.

Minutes and the webcast recording are published as soon as practical after the meeting. Minutes are unconfirmed until they are formally adopted at the next meeting of Council.

Council Meetings

Ordinary Council Meetings occur on the fourth Tuesday of the month*. (Excluding January and July*)

The next meeting is on 27 October 2026. 

Council meetings are held in the Council Chamber within the Shellharbour Civic Centre. 

Business Papers (Packets) 

Business papers for the next Council meeting will be available from the Thursday prior to the meeting date (see below).

Business papers and minutes for meetings prior to 2015 can be obtained under the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009 by completing an Access to Information form available on the Access to information page. In most cases, documents can be provided in hard copy or electronically.

Attending a Council Meeting

Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. No registration is required to attend.

Before attending a Council meeting, please read the Public Gallery Conduct Standards and Code of Meeting Practice.

Addressing Council (Public Forum)

Addresses to Council (on items listed in the Agenda as Item 10 only) are heard from 4.45pm on the day of the Council Meeting. You can register to speak from the time the Business Paper is published until 10am on the day of the meeting.

To register to speak on a listed matter in the Business Paper under Item 10, complete the  Public Forum Addresses Declaration - Form and return it to Corporate.Meetings@shellharbour.nsw.gov.au before 10am on the day of the meeting. We also encourage you to review the  Public Forum section of our Code of Meeting Practice 

If you are unable to complete the form online, come into or call Council on 4221 6111 and register to speak with a member of staff. You will still need to complete the Declaration prior to addressing Council.

Live streaming and recording

Meetings of the Council are live streamed and recorded. Open the meeting link in the Current Meetings or Previous Meetings for completed meetings.

Minutes and the webcast recording are published as soon as practical after the meeting. Minutes are unconfirmed until they are formally adopted at the next meeting of Council.
